title: Fixed 29-layer HfO2/MgF2 Fabry-Perot bandpass with thickness optimization
scientific_hypothesis: A symmetric 29-layer Fabry-Perot structure with HfO2/MgF2 quarter-wave mirrors and a half-wave HfO2 cavity, optimized for layer thicknesses, can achieve high transmission in 255-280 nm while suppressing 300-700 nm and 700-1100 nm bands without exceeding 30 layers.
design_principle: Quarter-wave optical thickness stacks create high reflectance bands centered at the design wavelength; a half-wave cavity layer between two mirror stacks creates a transmission peak within the reflectance band. The mirror pair count controls stopband width and depth, while cavity thickness controls passband center and width.
soft_objectives: maximize mean transmittance in 255-280 nm band
minimize mean transmittance in 300-700 nm band
minimize mean transmittance in 700-1100 nm band
maintain total layer count at exactly 29
manufacturing_considerations: all layers must be physically realizable thicknesses (10-200 nm range typical for UV coatings)
HfO2 and MgF2 are conventional evaporatable/sputterable dielectrics
total layer count 29 is within the 30-layer constraint
theory_basis: Quarter-wave optical thickness (n*d = lambda/4) creates constructive interference for reflection at the design wavelength
Fabry-Perot cavity with half-wave optical thickness creates transmission resonance within a high-reflectance stopband
Higher refractive index contrast between H and L materials produces wider and deeper stopbands
Symmetric mirror stacks on both sides of cavity produce symmetric passband shape
MgF2 has low refractive index (~1.38-1.40) and good UV transparency down to ~150 nm
HfO2 has moderate-high refractive index (~2.0-2.1) in UV and is commonly used for UV coatings
Stopband width scales with index ratio nH/nL; more pairs increase stopband depth
expected_advantages: Fixed topology allows clean isolation of thickness optimization effects
29 layers provides sufficient mirror pairs (7 per side) for deep stopbands in visible/NIR
HfO2/MgF2 pair has adequate index contrast for UV bandpass applications
Symmetric design should produce clean passband without sidelobes
known_risks: Refractive index values for HfO2 and MgF2 at 255-280 nm are recalled estimates; actual n/k data from the registry may differ and affect quarter-wave thickness calculations
Material absorption in deep UV (especially HfO2) is uncertain from memory; k values from registry will determine actual transmission limits
Quarter-wave thickness estimates (~32 nm for HfO2, ~48 nm for MgF2 at 267.5 nm) are approximate and will be tuned by the optimizer
Cavity layer being single HfO2 may not provide optimal passband width; multi-layer cavity could be better but would require different topology
Angle of incidence not specified in request; assumed normal incidence but space platform may have off-axis rays
Polarization effects not addressed; s and p polarization may split at non-normal incidence
Did not explore alternative material pairs (Al2O3/MgF2, SiO2/HfO2) which might have better UV transmission or index contrast
Did not explore different layer counts (25, 27, 30) which might offer better performance within constraint
execution_request_english: Optimize a 29-layer thin-film stack on SiO2 (Gao) substrate with air incidence. Layer sequence from air to substrate: HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2 (cavity), MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2. All 29 layer thicknesses are optimizable variables. Wavelength bands: maximize transmittance in 255-280 nm, minimize transmittance in 300-700 nm, minimize transmittance in 700-1100 nm. Normal incidence, unpolarized light. No metal layers. Total layer count fixed at 29.
